messages.author: c9959328f1f36ff7
messages.subject: too large data set?
parts:
Hi!:)

I have one more issue (hope it is the last one!)

We trapped small mammals on 8 sites, for 4 years. So far, I was fitting models for sites separetely (to make it faster). Now, I realized that I will be not able to summarize AICs (different no of sessions at sites = different no of parameters). 
I need to fit "global" (for all sites at once) model. 

However, when bulding the capthist file with read.capthist I'm getting the error: 

Error in matrix(0, nrow = nID, ncol = nocc) : 
  invalid 'ncol' value (too large or NA)
In addition: Warning message:
In w[indices[ord, , drop = F]] <- values[ord] :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

Data file has more then 5k rows. When I just cut half of the rows from the middle secr bulids the capthist file with no problems. 
I interpret it as having too large dataset, but it kind of does not make sense - I am sure, that someone before me have more data:)

Any ideas?

best,
Michał

messages.author: 118cea91a1619106
messages.subject: Re: too large data set?
parts:
This seems to be a problem with the number of occasions (it's not saying you have too much data, although you may later find it takes an awfully long time to process!). Probably the issue is in the second half of your data...

I am only guessing, but you may be able to fix it by specifying the number of occasions explicitly. The help says "The noccasions argument is needed only if there were no detections on the final occasion; it may be a positive integer (constant across all sessions) or a vector of positive integers, one for each session". Let me know if the problem won't go away!

Murray

messages.author: c9959328f1f36ff7
messages.subject: Re: too large data set?
parts:
Hi Murray!

thanks for your fast reply. I was trying to fit the models site by site to make it go faster, but in the end I need the global model (I will fix myself an access to super-computer;)).
Before that I need to clear the problems...


I tried to specify the noccasions, but it does not help. 

When I go with noccasions = 5 (I have 5 occasions in each session) it says:

Error in w[indices[ord, , drop = F]] <- values[ord] : 
  subscript out of bounds

The same problems occurs when I use smaller dataset. Unless I set noccasions for any number higher then 5. Then, in case of smaller datasets it works fine, but in case of global dataset it says:

Error in w[indices[ord, , drop = F]] <- values[ord] : 
  NAs are not allowed in subscripted assignments

In addition: Warning message:
In w[indices[ord, , drop = F]] <- values[ord] :
  number of items to replace is not a multiple of replacement length

So now, I have even one more problem :)
1. I still don't know how to load the global file
2. I do not understand the problem with noccasions...

This is the piece of code that I am using to run this:

all_years = read.capthist('all_datax.csv', 
                          'detectors.csv', detector = "multi", fmt = "trapID", covnames = c("sex"), noccasions = 5)

I am happy to send the csv file if it would help.

Thanks for your patience and helpfulness!:)
